_note: Back sides of Italy '43 counters read from counters-backs.jpg (11 rows x 10 columns = 110 counters, cell rNcM = row N from top, column M from left) and the unpunched markers on markers-1.jpg / markers-2.jpg. Every value was read from 3-4x crops in bz/. a-d-m and tr are as printed on the back; sp = boxed stacking value (null = none printed); quality: elite = red box, low = white box, null = normal. corner = number printed in the corner (campaign start hex or entry turn); cornerBox blue = starts frozen. All 67 unit backs carry a white vertical reduced stripe; ASU backs read "Fired 0 (1) 5" with no range printed. differences compare with data/italy43/oob.json. Counts: 67 unit backs, 25 ASU Fired sides, 9 remnants, 8 markers, 1 counter face up on its front (142/36).

uncertain: US-142-36: the counter in r1c10 is face up on its FRONT (6-6-3, sp 3, corner 17, no reduced stripe); its back was not photographed. By analogy with 141/36 and 143/36 it is probably 4-4-3 sp 3.
GE-5Geb-ASU: the size on the Fired side looks like plain "III" without brackets (other German division ASUs show "[III]"); medium confidence.

Remnant pairs: only one side of each remnant is in this photo. The infantry<->motorized pairing for German REM A-E and British REM A-C is inferred from oob (set-up cards) and should be confirmed from the fronts photo, especially REM E.
Backs of US REM A-C, 82 REM, 22/7A REM and French REM A-B are not in this photo; one of them may be the reverse of the 6/1A REM.

Front quality: most German battalions oob marks elite (I/115, I/129, II/129, 33, 26, 129, I/67, II/67, II/9, II/64, I/2/HG, 215) have plain defense on the back. Either they lose elite status when reduced or the oob elite flags need checking on the fronts.
